about.what: Concepts, doctrines, practices, states and opposites of aliveness, with the terms the library uses for them, corpus counts by work date and tradition, verbatim passages, and typed relations each carrying provenance.
about.counts: Pages that print any of a node's search phrases (Atlas Search phrase match, translation and OCR text, page_number > 0, case-folded, not accent-folded). The book facet returns the top 1,000 books by matching pages; dates and traditions are computed over live books in that facet. `pages_translation` counts the English translation alone.
about.work_dates: Per book, books.source_work_dates_meta.work.year (schema 2, #6721), the date the work was written; its basis is wikidata, author_lifespan, title_page or colophon (sourced) or model_knowledge. A book without one falls back to /root/aliveness/dated-works.jsonl, books.source_work_dates (one composition, no compilation), books.original_work_year, then the edition year. Each count records its basis; `sourced_pages` counts the dated pages with a sourced basis, and `by_century_edition` places the same pages by the printed edition.
about.gloss_and_edges: Node glosses, traditions and eras, and every edge claim, are scholarly background written by claude-opus-5-5. An edge is `passage` only when a judge found a page in the library that states it; the passage is quoted verbatim and linked.
about.terms: Forms are the seed spellings with their tagged-page counts in the page-terms harvest (#4695). Variants, equivalents and related terms come from src/data/concept-aliases.json where the node is a curated concept, otherwise from term-gloss bridges judged under .claude/docs/concept-aliases/JUDGE-RUBRIC.md. Related terms are never merged.
about.quotes: Every quote is a verbatim substring of the page's English translation after editorial wrappers and translator notes are removed; [square brackets] are the translator's inline glosses.
